neighbourhoods.name: Ramsey

housing: Huntingdonshire is a large, mainly rural district in western Cambridgeshire, with the market towns of Huntingdon, St Neots, St Ives, Ramsey and Godmanchester and many villages. Most homes are owner-occupied semis and detached houses on estates built since the 1960s, when the towns grew to take London overspill, alongside historic centres with period houses. Large new developments are being built at Alconbury Weald and around St Neots. RAF and US Air Force bases and commuting to Cambridge and London add to rental demand.
checkinTips: Riverside homes in St Ives, Huntingdon, Godmanchester and St Neots: look for signs of past flooding from the Great Ouse or damp in ground-floor rooms.
Fen-edge homes around Ramsey and Somersham: check for cracks and sticking doors that can come from shrinking clay or peat soils.
Period houses in the old town centres: record sash windows, beams, open fireplaces and damp at the base of walls.
New-build homes at Alconbury Weald and Loves Farm: note snagging still outstanding, meter readings and parking allocations.
Post-war estate houses in Huntingdon and St Neots: record the boiler, windows and doors, and the state of gardens, sheds and fencing.
tenantHelp: Tenants with disrepair, damp or safety problems in a private let can contact Huntingdonshire District Council's environmental health (private sector housing) team, after first reporting the problem to their landlord.
